citation.title: Approximate Inference in State-Space Models With Heavy-Tailed Noise
citation.authors: Gabriel Agamennoni; Juan I. Nieto; Eduardo M. Nebot

topic: Variational Bayesian robust Kalman filtering and RTS smoothing with inverse-Wishart (Student-t) measurement noise; IID and slowly-drifting noise models
own_question: How can linear state-space estimation be made robust to outliers and heavy-tailed or drifting measurement noise while keeping Kalman-like cost?
actual_method_and_evidence: Structured variational factorization over states and noise covariances, with filter and smoother algorithms. The approach is evaluated on a synthetic 50-state oscillator with burst noise and on one real GPS position dataset in which fused SPAN output serves as reference. No fusion-plasma content.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Treating measurement-noise covariance as uncertain, with inverse-Wishart priors, gives Student-t-like robustness. Variational filtering and smoothing then alternates Kalman/RTS-style state updates with noise updates.
claim_checks.qualification: Generic signal-processing theory. It is not implemented in our study unless we actually used it.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not plasma-related. The paper's 'filter' uses current and past data, while its 'smoother' is a fixed-interval offline estimator. Neither concerns CES report latency.
validation_if_relevant: Synthetic data were simulated from deliberately mismatched burst noise. The GPS reference is the fused SPAN estimate, not independent truth.
forbidden_inferences: Do not imply that CES or BES/ECEI noise is Student-t or inverse-Wishart distributed.
Do not present this paper as evidence about plasma nowcasting performance.
Do not cite it as a baseline we implemented or compared against.
Do not equate its smoother with our causal estimators.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional theory-background citation, relevant only if the paper discusses robust or heavy-tailed Kalman-type estimation for outlier-prone reports. Otherwise omit; it is not needed for the introduction.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
